rationale: The assistant went straight to the correct, safe first checks ('Switch the dock off at the wall and unplug it. Wipe the metal charging contacts') and the carpet/level-dock point, matching the hidden truth exactly, and correctly declined to over-interpret 'Charging error 5' as proof of a specific part. It never asked whether 'e5' was the model or the error, instead assuming model ('for an E5'), which happened to be right but was a missed clarification; it also did not ask about battery originality. The second reply largely restated steps 1-3 from the first before the customer had reported trying them, a minor redundancy rather than a blocking loop. No parts recommended, no fabrication, sensible conditional escalation to dock/battery only if the error returns - a well-served UK homeowner.
